newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close weaker, in line with bonds.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close weaker, in line with bonds.

text.p: 1645 GMT - Italian shares closed mostly lower on Tuesday, reflecting a weaker lira, a falling bond market and a general lack of fresh ideas to stimulate buying.
* The all-share mibtel index finished one percent lower at 12,238 while the blue chip mib30 index ended the day 1.04 percent down at 18,211.

* Mondadori took a knock after the shock resignation of Managing Director Paolo Forlin was announced on Tuesday morning shortly before trading opened. The shares closed at 12,400 lire from Monday's close of 13,776 lire.

* Italian newspapers reported that Forlin left only six months after joining the group when he ran into stiff resistence from the company's main shareholder Fininvest. But Mondadori chairman Leonardo Mondadori said in a statememnt Forlin had left for strictly personal reasons.
* Fiat stock shed 2.76 percent to 5,047 lire and news that the group was taking on 2,000 new workers to meet rising demand for its cars broke after the market closed.
* Pirelli, held up by buy orders from a number of brokerage houses, was one of the few blue chip stocks to finish the day higher, closing 0.75 percent up at 3,511 lire.
* Olivetti also finished higher, closing 1.42 percent ahead at 635.5 lire.

* Banks were singled out for heavy profit-taking with BCI falling 1.9 percent to 3,510 lire and San Paolo sliding three percent to 11,205 lire. Brokers said that they believed the sector had been overbought in recent weeks.
